Structuring a Go project effectively is fundamental to long-term maintainability, team collaboration, and scalability. Unlike frameworks that enforce rigid directory layouts, Go embraces flexibility—but with that freedom comes the responsibility to choose patterns that serve your project's specific needs.
Go's minimalist design philosophy extends to project organization. The language doesn't mandate a specific structure, instead trusting developers to make informed decisions. If you're building a fintech, healthcare, or enterprise React Native app, you've probably faced this question: How do I automatically log users out after they've been inactive?
It sounds simple. It isn't.
Regulatory frameworks like PCI-DSS, HIPAA, and SOC2 require automatic session termination after periods of inactivity. Beyond compliance, it's just good security—an unattended phone with an open banking app is a liability.
The requirements are straightforward:
Detect when a user stops interacting with the app
Show a warning before the session expires
Log them out if they don't respond
Handle edge cases like backgrounding, multitasking, and device sleep

Burnout Is a Signal of Internal Imbalance, Not Weakness
Why Surface-Level Self-Care Fails
The Gut–Brain–Immune Connection in Burnout
Redefining Self-Care Through a Holistic Approach
Nervous System Regulation
Consistent routines, mindful breathing, and reduced stimulation help calm the stress response and support emotional stability.
Digestive Healing
Warm, nourishing meals, proper meal timing, and gut-friendly nutrition strengthen digestion and nutrient absorption — essential for autoimmune balance.
Autoimmune-Supportive Nutrition
Anti-inflammatory, gut-healing foods reduce immune stress and support long-term wellness.
Restorative Sleep
Balanced digestion and a calm nervous system are critical for deep, healing sleep.
Sustainable Daily Routines
True self-care is practiced daily — not occasionally — creating stability for both mind and body.
From Burnout to Balance: A Sustainable Path Forward
A Gut-Focused, Autoimmune-Aware Healing Philosophy
Burnout is not a failure.
It is the body asking for balance.
